verdicts.reason: Quote states existing blocks may be used directly without user signals; scenario can exercise it.
Descriptive statement of adaptability; nothing to verify or exercise. Also duplicates the second half of the same quote.

One request and one response per cycle and no bursts is inherent to the channel structure (one beat per cycle); the no-burst part is checkable from interface signals, but the 'at most one per cycle' is a description of protocol width. Actor should be master/slave-agnostic but check is better as scenario/both since no-burst is checked via transaction size/length.
Descriptive statement about topology flexibility; nothing to verify.
Quote states interoperability of extended with base blocks; testable by scenario.

Baseline receiver ignoring user signals is a requirement; actor should be the receiver. 'destination' is acceptable but the behaviour is checkable as scenario (user signal changes do not affect behaviour).
Quote states baseline source generates a project-specific default user value; scenario check.
Descriptive statement that blocks can be modified; nothing to verify.

duplicates.reason: Both derive from the same quote about reuse of existing blocks; 02 is also rejected.

questions.question: What is the project-specific default value that a baseline source drives on the user signals? It is unspecified, so the check cannot be concrete.
Does 'no burst transactions' mean every request is a single beat, so the size field never exceeds the bus width? Please define the checkable condition.
